title: RuneScape Deleted the Wilderness for Three Years
hook: On December 10, 2007 Jagex removed PvP from the Wilderness and capped trading to fight gold sellers. It took 1.2 million votes and three years to undo it. Were you still playing when the Wilderness came back?
script: Did you know RuneScape once removed player versus player combat from the Wilderness for more than three years? On December 10, 2007, Jagex took PvP out of the Wilderness and announced a strict trade limit. The goal was to stop real world trading, where people sold gold and items for actual money. In its place, Jagex opened the Duel Arena to free players and added Bounty Hunter and Clan Wars. Dangerous ghosts called revenants roamed the Wilderness instead of other players. From January 2, 2008, the trade limit applied to every account in the game. Players hated it, and the community never stopped asking for the old game back. In December 2010, Jagex opened a petition. It pulled in over 1.2 million votes within 24 hours and passed 1.7 million before it closed. Jagex then ran a proper referendum that required a login to vote. It closed on January 14, 2011, with more than 1.2 million votes, and 91 percent of them said yes. On February 1, 2011, the Wilderness and free trade came back. Two years later, a similar vote brought Old School RuneScape to life. Did you ever lose your gear in the old Wilderness? Follow for more gaming history.
